title: Platform: client portal, communications, agent control, reports, closing, settings
summary: The firm-wide and client-facing parts of the app. Clients get a portal for messages, shared documents, bills, e-sign and secure upload. Staff get a single communications log fed by a generic mail connector, one approvals inbox for every human gate, an agent audit trail, ask-the-agent chat with citations, and automation settings. Reports, matter closing and archiving, and firm settings (roles, practice areas, integrations, Canadian data residency, export) complete the area.

screens.agent: Triages incoming client messages: it answers routine status questions from the matter brief using approved templates, drafts substantive replies for approval, and chases outstanding document requests. It classifies and files uploads, and posts a portal notice when a bill is issued or a signature is needed.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves any agent-drafted message that gives advice, contains new facts, or commits the firm to anything, and any agent-proposed document share (G-PM).
states: matter closed (read-only for 90 days, then hidden)
edge: Joint clients: a message to one client is visible to the other; show a warning and require the audience to be chosen explicitly
Opposing party or another third party is invited by mistake: block invitations to contacts who hold an adverse role on the matter
A client forwards their login: use MFA and a one-time link on new devices
An upload is infected or a type that is not allowed: reject it, tell the client, and store nothing
Client sends privileged content from an employer's email or device: show a privilege hint at portal sign-up (verify wording with LSO guidance)
Matter under an ethical wall: staff behind the wall cannot see portal threads
Client opens the portal from a phone or the mobile web; every tab must work at phone width
Two portal participants on one matter disagree (separating spouses); the agent flags any share that would reach both and routes it to G-PM
Notice email bounces: show 'client not notified' on the item and suggest a text or call
Matter closed: portal turns read-only for a set period, then access ends; client is told in the closing letter
Stage changes: the client gets a content-free notice; the stage text shown is the approved client label, never the internal name
A participant is added mid-matter: earlier messages and documents stay hidden unless staff choose to share history
A bill is re-issued: content-free notice to the client; staff see the bill version history
Phone-width upload: camera capture with page-edge detection, installable web app with web push and passkeys stand in for a native app
screens.reg: RPC 3.3 confidentiality. Joint-retainer disclosure, RPC 3.4 (verify). PIPEDA consent and safeguards. Messages that give advice are the lawyer's responsibility (RPC 3.1, 6.1).

edge: The document is edited after it was sent: void the request automatically and require approval again
A signer's email bounces: alert staff and do not retry silently
A document needs a commissioner, a witness or a wet signature (for example some affidavits or wills): block e-sign and say why (verify which Ontario documents are excluded)
The client signs on behalf of a corporation: record their signing authority

screens.agent: Pulls mail through the generic mail connector (IMAP/SMTP or a mail API configured as an integration), threads it, matches it to a matter, files the attachments, extracts deadlines, tasks and time, flags possible privilege, and drafts replies. It also summarizes calls when a transcript with recorded consent exists.
screens.gate: Outgoing substantive or client-facing email (G-OUT). Call or meeting summaries before they become the record. Deadlines and time entries go to their own gates (G7, G9).
edge: One email concerns two matters: file it to both and record why
The sender is an adverse party writing directly to the client's lawyer: flag this for the no-contact rule check (RPC 7.2-6, verify)
Reply-all includes opposing counsel or an unknown domain: hard warning before sending
The mailbox connector loses auth: banner plus an admin alert; mail that arrives in the gap is backfilled
Personal email in a lawyer's mailbox: a never-file rule by sender or folder
Call recorded without consent: the transcript is not ingested
Email filed to a matter the sender is walled from: block and alert compliance
Large attachment over the mail size limit: send a portal link instead
Same email arrives through two users' mailboxes: de-duplicate by message id
Auto-reply / out-of-office mail: file as noise, never extract deadlines from it
Sync scope widened or narrowed: the agent shows a preview (N items would be unfiled, M filed) and nothing changes until a human confirms; logged as an agent event
Attachments of filed mail land in the matter's 'Email attachments' folder with a link back to the message
Mail sent to a matter inbound address from an unregistered sender: rejected and logged, never filed
screens.reg: RPC 3.3 confidentiality and misdirected communications. Privilege. One-party consent for recording calls under the Criminal Code s.184 (verify), with firm policy requiring all-party notice. PIPEDA.

screens.agent: Creates each item with the evidence attached and a one-line 'what changes if you approve'. It orders the queue by deadline risk, chases overdue approvals, and after a decision either carries out the approved action or revises the draft using the rejection reason.
screens.gate: This screen is where every gate in the app is decided. The approver must be eligible for the gate type, and an agent can never approve.
edge: The source changed after the draft was made (for example, a new payment arrived): mark the item stale and require a re-draft
The approver is also the person who will benefit (for example, their own bill write-down): require a second approver (verify firm policy)
Two reviewers open the same item: soft lock with a takeover option
The approver leaves the firm: their items are reassigned to their supervisor automatically
Sole practitioner: the approver and the supervising licensee are the same person; allow it, but still require a reason on high-risk items
screens.reg: RPC 6.1 supervision: delegated and AI work is approved by a licensee. BL9: only authorized signatories approve trust withdrawals (verify). The audit trail must show who approved what and when.

screens.agent: Retrieves from the matter's documents, comms log, calendar and ledgers. It answers only from those sources (plus statute or rule text where the firm has enabled that), cites each claim, and refuses or says 'not in file' rather than guess. For a goal it proposes a step plan, runs internal steps, and stops at each regulated step for a human.
screens.gate: none for internal answers and internal steps. Every step that sends, files or moves money pauses for its own gate (G-OUT, G-PM or the area gate).
edge: The question needs facts from a walled matter: refuse without revealing that the matter exists
Conflicting sources (two different dates in the file): show both with citations and do not pick one
The user asks for legal research beyond the file: label it clearly as general research, not file fact
Answer cites a superseded document version: always cite the latest version and note that a superseded one exists
A step would send, file or move money: the run pauses there; the agent never skips or batches past a regulated step
User leaves the page mid-run: the run continues with internal steps only and the pending step waits in the approvals inbox
screens.reg: RPC 3.1 competence: the lawyer verifies AI output before relying on it. Matter data is stored in the Canadian cell; where model inference runs is shown on the data residency panel (integrations-data).
